reason: The passage extensively portrays multiple elite members unfavorably: Amnon (royal son) commits sexual assault against his sister; Absalom (prince) assassinates his brother, then deliberately manipulates the people and stages a rebellion against his own father the king; Ahithophel (royal advisor) provides counsel to depose the king and humiliate him through his concubines; Shimei (from Saul's former royal house) curses the king; even Joab (military commander) must be commanded to moderate his actions. Throughout chapters 13-19, those of high status are consistently shown engaging in betrayal, violence, manipulation, and disloyalty.
